title: Deactivating document may cause a null reference issue during reload
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

I believe that, during a reload, the step to deactivate the document may have a null reference.

---

The first step of [deactivate a document...](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#deactivate-a-document-for-a-cross-document-navigation) is as follows:

> Let navigable be displayedDocument's node navigable

Where the node navigable is defined as

> To get the node navigable of a node node, return the navigable whose active document is node's node document, or null if there is no such navigable.

And:

> A navigable's active document is its active session history entry's document.
> To get a session history entry's document, return its document state's document.

So, in all, the node navigable is a navigable whose active session history entry's document state's document is equal to the document (or null if there is no such document).

---

Directly under step 12 of [apply the history step](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#apply-the-history-step), it says:
> Let displayedEntry be navigable's active session history entry.
> Let targetEntry be navigable's current session history entry.

And earlier in the spec, the current session history entry was set as follows:
> Let targetEntry be the result of getting the target history entry given navigable and targetStep.
> Set navigable's current session history entry to targetEntry.

Because target step is the same as the active entry's step, I believe that the active and current entry end up being the same entry.

Anyways, in the case of a reload ("If targetEntry's document is null, or targetEntry's document state's reload pending is true"), we repopulate targetEntry's document ("In parallel, attempt to populate the history entry's document for targetEntry") to be the newly loaded document.

Population of the new document occurs before deactivation of the old document (because deactivation of the old document was queued for later in a continuation).

While populating the document, critically, we update the existing document state's document
> set entry's document state's document to the result of loading a document

Keep in mind, as established earlier, that the targetEntry, active entry, and current entry are all the same at this point!
As such, by mutating targetEntry's document state, we also change active entry's document state to point to a different document

So anyways, by the time [deactivate a document...](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#deactivate-a-document-for-a-cross-document-navigation) runs this line:
> Let navigable be displayedDocument's node navigable

There is no active entry's document state holding displayedDocument, as the active entry was mutated to have a different document. Since node navigable is indirectly defined in terms of that, the node navigable will be null!

So when we later get to a step that uses the navigable (like "Set the ongoing navigation for navigable"), the algorithm will crash because the navigable is null.

---

The fix would be really simple - the apply the history step already has a proper reference to the navigable, so pass that to the deactivation step instead of trying to determine the relevant navigable in the deactivation step.

---

Hopefully, I explained it well, my brain turns mush trying to reason through these specs

And of course, a whole bunch of threading shenanigans occur, but I believe that just makes the issue racey, as opposed to resolving it

(Unrelatedly, while I already happen to be opening an issue, I'd also like to mention that I believe steps 12.8.5 and 12.8.6 of the history step should be in the opposite order).
